players.name: Germie Bernard
players.waiver_note:
This article usually doesn't include players who are rostered in 50% or more of Yahoo leagues, but we're making an exception for Germie Bernard, who's rostered in exactly 50% of Yahoo leagues.

If Bernard is unrostered in one of your leagues, there's a good chance it's a shallow league with 10 or fewer teams or extremely short benches. Even if it's that type of a league, Bernard should be rostered.

Injuries to WRs Michael Pittman Jr. and Roman Wilson have thrust Bernard into a substantial role, and the second-round rookie appears ready for it. In the Steelers' 26-19 victory over the Buccaneers on Sunday, Bernard had 11-87-1 on 12 targets. He had a 27.3% target share in that contest.

The second-round rookie is going to be ranked inside the top 25 at receiver this week. If Bernard remains unrostered in your league, fix that.

players.name: Tre Tucker
players.waiver_note:
Tre Tucker will draw waiver attention this week after putting up 5-97-2 on seven targets against the Bills in Week 6.

Tucker has had a couple of splashy games, including a 5-119-1 performance against the Chargers in Week 2. But his floor has been surprisingly sturdy. Tucker has caught at least four passes and has topped 40 receiving yards in five consecutive games.

The Rams present a tough matchup in Week 7, but Tucker is nevertheless playable in a four-team bye week.

players.name: Keenan Allen
players.waiver_note:
Over his last three games, Keenan Allen has 19 catches for 190 yards on 29 targets. The 34-year-old Allen has drawn 11 more targets than fellow Colts WR Josh Downs over that stretch.

TE Tyler Warren missed the Colts' Week 6 game against the Titans with a groin injury, and his absence might have contributed to Allen's big target total. But Allen has become an important component in the Indy passing attack.

Allen has a nightmare matchup with the Vikings this week, but then he gets matchups with the pass-funnel Jacksonville defense and a Dallas defense that by most statistical measures has been the worst in the league.

It might be worth picking up Allen now, letting him ride your bench in Week 7, and then starting him in Weeks 8-9.

players.name: Omar Cooper Jr.
players.waiver_note:
In his first NFL game, Omar Cooper Jr. played just five offensive snaps and had a 30-yard catch on his only target before sustaining a high-ankle sprain that landed him on IR.

Cooper came off IR in Week 6 and had 6-103-1 on seven targets. His touchdown came on a 48-yard bomb. Cooper also had another touchdown negated by a dubious offensive pass interference penalty called against Jets WR Tim Patrick.

The 30th overall pick in this year's draft, Cooper is a hard-nosed gamer who has good hands and is dangerous after the catch. He can also line up either outside or inside. (Cooper played in the slot on Sunday when the Jets used three-receiver sets.)

Cooper probably isn't going to challenge Garrett Wilson's alpha receiver status on the Jets anytime soon, but he can be an effective No. 2 or No. 3.

Although the Jets will probably be getting Adonai Mitchell back from a finger injury in a week or two, Cooper could be a solution for WR-needy fantasy teams. He has playable matchups against the Dolphins and Raiders the next two weeks.

players.name: Tyler Higbee
players.waiver_note:
Davante Adams appeared to sustain a non-contact knee injury in the final minutes of the Rams' Week 6 loss to the Cardinals. The Rams already use a ton of two- and three-TE sets. If Adams misses significant time with his injury, it's a good bet that the Rams will lean hard into multiple tight end usage.

Higbee had a relatively disappointing 4-22-0 stat line on four targets vs. the Cardinals after racking up 18-212-1 on 23 targets over his previous three games.

The Rams have a Week 7 matchup against a Raiders defense that has been getting worked over by tight ends this season. If you need a tight end this week, go after Higbee. Spend an extra buck or two if we learn that Adams is going to be out for a while.

players.name: T.J. Hockenson
players.waiver_note:
T.J. Hockenson sustained a concussion in Week 5, so you'll want to check his status before bidding on him. But chances are he'll be ready to go in Week 7 when the Vikings come out of their bye week.

Hockenson has an appealing Week 7 matchup against the Colts, who entered Week 6 having given up the 10th-most fantasy points to tight ends. In Week 8, Hockenson gets an even better matchup against the Lions, who have allowed far and away the most fantasy points to TEs this year.

If you're streaming tight ends, Hockenson should be able to more than adequately cover you at the position for the next two weeks.

players.name: Kendre Miller
players.waiver_note:
Kendre Miller is in a New Orleans backfield committee that also includes Alvin Kamara and CJ Donaldson. Miller plays almost exclusively on early downs, and on Sunday he had a team-high 20 carries for 70 yards. He also had two catches on two targets, but those receptions gained zero yards.

The Saints' running game has been ineffective, partly due to subpar offensive line play. Miller is averaging 3.1 yards per carry.

But rushing volume is valuable — especially during the bye weeks — and Miller has logged 30 carries over the last two weeks. Travis Etienne (hamstring) is eligible to come off IR in Week 9. Until Etienne is back, Miller should continue to get decent, flex-level rushing volume. It helps that Saints head coach and playcaller Kellen Moore runs his offense at a fast pace.

A tricky but playable matchup against the Steelers awaits Miller this week, and then the Saints are on bye in Week 8.

Miller is no backfield savior, but he could be a useful depth piece until Etienne comes back and clogs the New Orleans backfield.

players.name: DeMario Douglas
players.waiver_note:
A.J. Brown returned from a high-ankle sprain on Sunday, but DeMario Douglas was the Patriots' most impactful pass catcher in Week 6, finishing with 7-86-1 on eight targets. Douglas has 151 receiving yards and three touchdowns over his last two games.

Brown's return might have been a blemish on the near-term fantasy value of Douglas, but Romeo Doubs sustained a shoulder injury Sunday while hauling in a long TD pass from Drake Maye, and if Doubs misses time, Douglas could have low-level flex value during a run of favorable matchups against the Bears, Dolphins and Packers.

players.name: Pat Freiermuth
players.waiver_note:
Pat Freiermuth has to share TE targets with Darnell Washington and hasn't produced more than 46 receiving yards in a game this season, but he has four touchdowns and is averaging 3.5 catches per contest.

If you need to stream a tight end and don't want to pay a lot for the privilege, spend a buck on Freiermuth and pray that he scores a touchdown against the Browns.

players.name: Jaylin Noel
players.waiver_note:
Second-year WR Jaylin Noel had the first 100-yard game of his career on Sunday, catching 4-of-4 targets for 107 yards and a touchdown against the Jaguars in London. Noel had a 13-yard touchdown on Sunday and has scored a TD in each of his last two games.

The arrival of Marvin Harrison Jr. via trade complicates the target outlook for Noel. Harrison played with Texans QB C.J. Stroud at Ohio State, so they have some chemistry. The Texans' Nico Collins is often a target hog, of course. Xavier Hutchinson is also involved, and Tank Dell could be close to a return from the catastrophic knee injury he sustained in December 2024.

But Noel figures to remain the Texans' primary slot receiver even after Dell comes back. A third-round pick out of Iowa State in 2025, Noel is an exceptional athlete who clocked a 4.39 in the 40-yard dash at the scouting combine and had a vertical jump of 41 1/2 inches.

Over his last three games, Noel has caught 12-of-12 targets for 233 yards and two touchdowns. He would have to grow his target share to become consistently fantasy-relevant, but Noel is an ascending player worth rostering in case he's on the verge of a breakthrough.

players.name: Michael Mayer
players.waiver_note:
The Raiders' passing attack is unconventional in that the team's No. 2 tight end is more fantasy-relevant than the No. 2 wide receiver.

Brock Bowers is not only the Raiders' No. 1 tight end, but the No. 1 tight end in the entire NFL. To Michael Mayer's credit, he's managing to thrive in Bowers' shadow. Mayer actually outproduced Bowers in Week 6, with 7-95-0 on nine targets against the Bills. Bowers had 4-70-0 on nine targets.

Mayer is averaging 5.7 targets, 4.7 catches and 44.7 receiving yards per game. He's playable in a pinch this week and can be a solid backup tight end in leagues where rostering more than one TE makes sense.

players.name: Kendrick Bourne
players.waiver_note:
With Marvin Harrison Jr. deactivated for the Cardinals' Week 5 game and traded away to Houston before their Week 6 game, Kendrick Bourne has had 10-117-0 on 16 targets the last two weeks.

Now the No. 2 receiver for the pass-heavy Cardinals, Bourne can be a useful asset, particularly in PPR leagues. With 22 touchdowns in 133 career games, Bourne has never been a prolific TD scorer. But reception volume should keep Bourne fantasy viable.

Bourne's matchup against Denver this week is no picnic, but then he gets a fantastic matchup against the Cowboys and their asbestos pass defense in Week 8.

players.name: Roschon Johnson
players.waiver_note:
With Kyle Monangai sidelined by turf toe for a second straight week, Roschon Johnson once again backed up starting RB D'Andre Swift in Week 6 and had 13-51-1 rushing and 2-34-0 receiving on two targets against the Falcons.

Monangai could miss another week or two. It would be a stretch to project Johnson for another 15 touches against the Patriots in Week 7. The Bears ran 77 offensive plays and held the ball for just over 40 minutes of clock time in their Week 6 win over the Falcons, which pumped up Johnson's workload.

Still, the Bears have one of the better rushing attacks in the league, and Johnson might be flex-worthy in deeper leagues this week with four teams on bye.

players.name: Colby Parkinson
players.waiver_note:
As noted above in the Tyler Higbee report, the injury to Davante Adams could lead to additional targets for the Rams' tight ends.

Colby Parkinson played 12 fewer snaps and ran 10 fewer routes than Higbee in Week 6, but Parkinson had the better numbers, with 5-31-1 on six targets.

With Terrance Ferguson likely to return in Week 8, Parkinson will probably be third in the pass-catching pecking order among the Rams' tight ends. Still, Parkinson could have streaming value in the coming weeks if Adams is out of the picture for a while.

players.name: Ja'Kobi Lane
players.waiver_note:
Promising rookie Ja'Kobi Lane returned from a wrist injury Sunday and had 4-40-0 on five targets.

A third-round pick from USC, Lane was a standout in training camp. Longtime Ravens beat writer Jamison Henley wrote that in his 27 years of covering the team, Lane had one of the best performances he had seen from any Baltimore rookie.

In his first game back from injury, Lane played 54.4% of the Ravens' offensive snaps, finishing third in WR targets behind Zay Flowers and Devontez Walker. Flowers is the unquestioned No. 1 receiver in Baltimore. Walker, despite his 37 offensive snaps in Week 6, had zero catches on two targets.

Rashod Bateman injured his shoulder on Sunday. If Bateman misses time, Lane will be assured of being on the field in three-receiver sets, and it probably won't take much for Lane to pass Walker on the depth chart, based on how much buzz there was about Lane this summer.

Lane's Week 6 numbers might have looked even better if Lamar Jackson had played, but Jackson's ankle injury forced the Ravens to play Tyler Huntley at quarterback in a 13-10 loss to the Browns. Jackson is likely to return this week.

Lane is a good speculative addition.

players.name: Bam Knight
players.waiver_note:
Bam Knight had 15-80-0 rushing and 2-18-0 on two targets for the Cardinals in their Week 6 upset of the Rams.

It was an unexpectedly run-friendly game script for the Cardinals, with Arizona running 72 offensive plays, and Knight and Tyler Allgeier combining for 33 carries. Allgeier out-snapped Knight 40-32.

Whatever fantasy value Knight has most likely evaporates as soon as rookie RB Jeremiyah Love returns from an ankle injury — and that could happen this week.

But if Love misses another game, Knight could be a flex option against a Broncos defense that has had trouble tackling and has given up 26.0 half-point PPR fantasy points per game to RBs.

players.name: Samaje Perine
players.waiver_note: Samaje Perine is unlikely to take Chase Brown's starting job in Cincinnati, but it was eye-opening when Perine out-carried Brown 14-13 in the Bengals' Week 5 win over the Dolphins. Perine was also more effective with his carries in that game, averaging 4.9 yards per carry, while Brown averaged 3.0. Perine is one of the more essential handcuff RBs, and we can't completely discount the possibility that he turns the Bengals' backfield into a timeshare.

players.name: Rashid Shaheed
players.waiver_note: Rashid Shaheed will draw some waiver interest after producing 5-66-0 on eight targets against the Broncos last Thursday night. But those eight targets were a season high for Shaheed, who hadn't caught more than three passes or produced more than 35 receiving yards in any of his previous five games. Seahawks QB Sam Darnold threw 51 passes against the Broncos last week, and the unusually high pass volume inflated Shaheed's stat line. Don't chase the dragon here.

players.name: Mike Washington Jr.
players.waiver_note: Ashton Jeanty has been banged up all season. If Jeanty were to miss any time, rookie Mike Washington Jr. would assume a big workload for Las Vegas. A fourth-round pick out of Arkansas, the 6-1, 223-pound Washington is a size-speed freak who clocked a 4.33 at the scouting combine.

players.name: Christian Kirk
players.waiver_note:
With Deebo Samuel out with a hamstring injury and promising rookie De'Zhaun Stribling not expected to return from an ankle injury until the latter part of November, Christian Kirk could play a meaningful short-term role for the 49ers' high-powered offense.

Kirk strained his calf on the first day of San Francisco's training camp and has been on IR. He has been designated to return from IR, and if he doesn't make his return against the Commanders on Monday night, he'll almost certainly suit up against the Falcons in Week 7.

Since his 1,100-yard season with the Jaguars in 2022 and a productive but injury-shortened campaign with the Jags in 2023, Kirk hasn't done much. He had 27-379-1 over eight games with Jacksonville in 2024 and 28-239-1 over 13 games with the Texans last year. Kirk averaged just 4.6 yards per target and 0.90 yards per route run in 2025.

Kirk, who turns 30 next month, could have a substantial role in one of the most efficient passing attacks in the league this week when the 49ers face a pass-funnel Falcons defense.

players.name: Caleb Douglas
players.waiver_note: The Dolphins have a league-low 849 passing yards and two touchdown passes through five games, but they have an intriguing pair of rookie receivers in Chris Bell and Caleb Douglas. Bell, who has an appealing combination of size (6-2, 228) and speed, might have been a first-round pick instead of a late third-rounder had he not torn his ACL last November while playing for Louisville. Douglas, a third-round pick from Texas Tech, was a standout in training camp and had 5-94-0 in Week 1 before sustaining an ankle injury in Week 2 that landed him on IR. He is expected to return this week as the Dolphins emerge from a Week 6 bye. Bell and Douglas are intriguing talents who might be worth stashing in case the Dolphins' passing game starts to show a pulse.

players.name: Chris Bell
players.waiver_note: The Dolphins have a league-low 849 passing yards and two touchdown passes through five games, but they have an intriguing pair of rookie receivers in Chris Bell and Caleb Douglas. Bell, who has an appealing combination of size (6-2, 228) and speed, might have been a first-round pick instead of a late third-rounder had he not torn his ACL last November while playing for Louisville. Douglas, a third-round pick from Texas Tech, was a standout in training camp and had 5-94-0 in Week 1 before sustaining an ankle injury in Week 2 that landed him on IR. He is expected to return this week as the Dolphins emerge from a Week 6 bye. Bell and Douglas are intriguing talents who might be worth stashing in case the Dolphins' passing game starts to show a pulse.

players.name: Emmett Johnson
players.waiver_note: Chiefs rookie Emmett Johnson is a dual run-catch threat who would inherit a big workload in a top offense if anything happened to Kenneth Walker III. Johnson is rostered in only 23% of Yahoo leagues.

players.name: Tommy Tremble
players.waiver_note: Tommy Tremble had a pair of TD catches for the Panthers on Sunday. Although Tremble led the Carolina tight ends in snaps, routes and targets in Week 6, Tremble is not worth your attention. He's had 25 or fewer receiving yards in three of the Panthers' first five games.

players.name: Jaleel McLaughlin
players.waiver_note:
Whatever fantasy value Jaleel McLaughlin has is fragile and probably won't be long-lasting.

Quinshon Judkins missed Week 6 with an ankle injury. The Browns' other second-year running back, Dylan Sampson, has been out with a knee injury since Week 1, but he was back at practice last week and could be on the verge of a return.

With Judkins and Sampson out, McLaughlin played 61.9% of Cleveland's offensive snaps in Week 6 and had 9-41-0 rushing and 4-14-0 on four targets.

If Judkins is back this week, McLaughlin's fantasy value turns to dust. Even if Judkins and Sampson both remain out, McLaughlin would probably cede some early-down work in Week 7 to Audric Estime, who had a 30.2% snap share in Week 6 and had 9-19-1 rushing, getting a carry on nearly half of his 19 snaps.

Still, we have to mention McLaughlin as a waiver possibility in case he once again operates as Cleveland's lead back in Week 7. If he does, a matchup against the Titans would make McLaughlin a top-30 RB option in another four-team bye week.

players.name: Jaylen Wright
players.waiver_note: Ollie Gordon has seized command of Miami's lead-back role, but we shouldn't completely dismiss the possibility that Jaylen Wright plays a fantasy-relevant role at some point. Last season, it was often hard to discern whether Gordon or Wright was the top backup to De'Von Achane. It's clear that Gordon is ahead of Wright on the depth chart now, but it's worth keeping the speedy Wright on the radar and perhaps claiming him if you have a roster spot to spare.

players.name: Corey Kiner
players.waiver_note: Corey Kiner led the Patriots in Week 6 rushing yardage with 11-57-0 against the Jets. But it's hard to project Kiner for a fantasy-relevant role in a backfield that also includes Rhamondre Stevenson and TreVeyon Henderson.

players.name: Jonah Coleman
players.waiver_note:
Heading into Week 3, Jonah Coleman was a hot waiver pickup because it seemed as if J.K. Dobbins and RJ Harvey might both miss their next game with hamstring injuries, leaving Coleman with a lead-back role. It turned out Coleman had a high-ankle sprain that led to a stint on injured reserve (IR), while Dobbins and Harvey both played in Week 3.

Fantasy football can be a mischievous imp.

Coleman is eligible to come off IR this week and is expected to suit up for the Broncos' Week 7 game against the Cardinals. He won't command the sort of hefty FAAB bids he drew in Week 3, but Coleman is still worth your attention.

The Broncos' offense is stuck in the mud. Denver has averaged 196 yards of offense over its last two games and has exceeded 300 yards of offense in a game only once this season. QB Bo Nix bears a large share of the blame, but Dobbins is averaging 3.3 yards per carry, while Harvey is averaging 3.9.

The Denver offense could use a spark, and perhaps Coleman could provide it. The rookie from Washington had a strong training camp and looked good in Week 2, when he had 10-39-1 rushing and 3-19-0 receiving against the Jaguars, who have the NFL's best run defense by virtually any statistical measure. Perhaps it's no coincidence that the Broncos rolled up a season-high 392 yards of offense against the Jags that week with Coleman prominently involved.

Although he has the straight-line speed of a tight end, the 5-8, 220-pound Coleman is hard to tackle, has good rushing instincts, is an able pass catcher, and is regarded as a good pass blocker.

Coleman has been out of sight, out of mind during his stay on IR. This is a good chance to acquire a talented young RB who has a chance to have an impactful role for a team in desperate need of an offensive catalyst.

players.name: Jawhar Jordan
players.waiver_note: Elevated from the Texans' practice squad last week, Jawhar Jordan had a key 25-yard TD run in the Texans' Week 6 victory over the Jaguars as part of a 6-43-1 rushing day. Jordan also added a seven-yard catch. Jordan played only 22.2% of Houston's offensive snaps on Sunday, so you would have a hard time starting him with any confidence against the Giants in Week 7. The Texans are on bye in Week 8, and it's possible RB David Montgomery returns from his groin injury in Week 9, at which point the Texans' backfield presumably goes back to being a two-man platoon with Montgomery and Woody Marks. We don't recommend adding Jordan.

players.name: Adonai Mitchell
players.waiver_note:
Adonai Mitchell showed a spark early this season with 3-60-0 against the Titans in Week 1 and 6-63-0 on 12 targets against the Packers in Week 2, but a finger injury has kept Mitchell sidelined for the last four weeks.

Mitchell is likely to be back either this week or next. His impending return might have been more eagerly anticipated by waiver shoppers were it not for a dazzling Week 6 performance by rookie WR Omar Cooper Jr., who came off IR and had 6-103-1 on seven targets against the Patriots.

Mitchell might be worth a speculative addition, but keep the FAAB bids small.

players.name: Jordyn Tyson
players.waiver_note:
Jordyn Tyson has been on IR with a hamstring injury and could be back as early as this week. The more likely scenario is that he returns in Week 9, after the Saints' Week 8 bye.

Tyson was the eighth overall pick in this year's draft, and some draft analysts believe he's the most talented receiver in the rookie class. Tyson had a strong training camp before injuring his hamstring in a joint practice with the Jaguars. Durability was the biggest knock on Tyson coming out of college, since he had missed games with a variety of ailments.

The Saints have a high-volume passing game, and if Tyson can stay healthy, he could shine alongside star WR Chris Olave.

Tyson will only get more expensive once he's back. This might be your last chance to get him at a reasonable price.

players.name: Brian Robinson Jr.
players.waiver_note: Week 6 was a good reminder that Brian Robinson Jr.'s stand-alone value is fragile. After averaging 10.2 carries over his first five games, Robinson had just two carries for one yard Sunday against the Bears. Atlanta fell into a deep hole against Chicago, and a negative game script is not Robinson's friend. But Robinson remains one of the top handcuff RBs in fantasy football as an insurance policy for Bijan Robinson investors.

players.name: Jakobi Meyers
players.waiver_note:
Jakobi Meyers is now being rostered in under half of Yahoo leagues, and he probably won't be a popular waiver claim this week with the Jaguars on bye following their two-week residency in London.

A dependable eighth-year veteran, Meyers has 20-285-2 this season on 28 targets. Meyers had 5-83-0 on 10 targets against the Texans in Week 6, with season highs in targets and receiving yardage.

Parker Washington has become the Jaguars' clear No. 1 receiver, but Meyers is No. 2 ahead of the disappointing Brian Thomas. That's not a bad role when your quarterback is Trevor Lawrence and your playcaller is Liam Coen.

Meyers could be a useful depth piece if you don't mind adding a receiver who isn't playing this week.

players.name: Keon Coleman
players.waiver_note:
There's a good chance DJ Moore will be back from his shoulder injury when the Bills emerge from their Week 7 bye, but Keon Coleman could still be fantasy-relevant upon Moore's return.

Maybe this isn't a true third-year breakout for Coleman, but it's been at least a slight breakthrough for him. Coleman has scored a touchdown in three consecutive games. He has caught 79.2% of his 24 targets and is averaging 11.8 yards per target.

With the Bills on bye this week, you can probably acquire Coleman with a $1 or $2 bid and hope that this really is a third-year breakout and it's just getting started.

players.name: Terrance Ferguson
players.waiver_note: Terrance Ferguson is on IR with an ankle injury but is eligible to come off in Week 8. Ferguson flashed his plus athleticism with 6-54-1 on nine targets against the Giants in Week 2. He could be prominently involved in the Rams' passing game upon his return, particularly if WR Davante Adams misses time with the knee injury he sustained in Week 6.

players.name: Travis Hunter
players.waiver_note: Travis Hunter, the Jaguars' full-time cornerback and part-time wide receiver, had his most impactful pass-catching performance of the season on Sunday, with 4-59-1 on four targets. The second overall pick of the 2025 draft, Hunter is immensely talented but simply doesn't get enough offensive snaps to warrant a spot on your roster. Hunter did all that damage on only nine snaps in Week 6, and he now has six catches for the season.
